title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: MinLaw pandemic legal framework work
sections.summary: MinLaw and its partners enacted a legal framework to re-order unperformable obligations and simplify insolvency procedures during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the context of the Ministry of Law (MinLaw)'s work to build resilience, what was noteworthy during the pandemic was the stupendous amount of work done within a short span of time with its partners, including the Attorney-General Chambers, other Government bodies and the private sector, to enact a legal framework that re-ordered legal obligations that could not have been performed and simplify insolvency procedures.

sections.label: Chronicling MinLaw pandemic efforts
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MinLaw chronicle its and its partners' pandemic-period efforts so future generations benefit from the legal lessons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In these circumstances and with a view to ensure that future generations of Singaporeans will benefit from the legal lessons and insights gained from this unique experience, I would like to suggest that the MinLaw chronicle the efforts of itself and its partners over the pandemic period.

sections.label: Suggesting Singapore accede Convention
sections.summary: Some years back, the speaker suggested that Singapore accede to this Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Some years back, I suggested that Singapore accede to this Convention.

sections.label: Easier enforcement of Court judgments
sections.summary: In November 2022, the Minister said his Ministry is working with MSF and the Courts to make enforcement of civil and family Court judgments easier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In November 2022, the hon Minister informed this House that his Ministry is working with stakeholders, such as the Minister of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Courts, to make enforcement of civil and family Court judgments easier.

sections.label: Amending rules for PHCs
sections.summary: In November 2022, the speaker suggested amending applicable rules to let PHCs summarily determine and dispose of frivolous and vexatious claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In November 2022, I suggested that applicable rules be amended to allow PHCs to summarily determine and dispose of frivolous and vexatious claims.

sections.label: Court-based mediation at CDRT
sections.summary: The speaker proposes Court-based mediation where parties must first undergo Court-led mediation when action is commenced at CDRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If HDB is not able to resolve the dispute, it would often advise residents that they can refer the matter for mediation at the Community Mediation Centre (CMC) or even for resolution at the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, as mediation at CMC requires the agreed participation of both parties to a dispute, many such disputes do not stand a chance of being resolved by mediation, simply because one of the parties opts out of mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While I understand why mediation should be voluntary and while I do understand that mediation may not always be suitable for every dispute, I feel that for a good number of cases, it is a good opportunity wasted for parties to try and resolve their differences during mediation, when parties have the option to opt out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I propose that we adopt a Court-based mediation where parties first have to go through a Court-led mediation when action is commenced at CDRT.

sections.label: Review of CDRT process
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to review the CDRT process to make it more user-friendly for laypeople of different educational backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, I have a few suggestions in respect of the CDRT process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to review the CDRT process, and see whether the system and procedure can be made more user-friendly for laypeople of different educational backgrounds.

sections.label: Making CDRT less intimidating
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the review can make the process less intimidating and more user-friendly for people not proficient in English and for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can we also review to see how we can make it less intimidating and more user-friendly for people who are not proficient in English, as well as for our seniors?

sections.label: Feedback on community dispute framework
sections.summary: The speaker says residents' feedback is that the current community dispute resolution framework is not effective, with errant neighbours not complying with CDRT orders or flouting mediation agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Notwithstanding our efforts, the feedback I have received from residents in such situations is that the current community dispute resolution framework is not effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: They shared that errant neighbours do not comply with the orders of the CDRT or flout a mediation agreement.

sections.label: Stricter enforcement and inter-Ministry review
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Minister will review policy to increase compliance with orders and agreements, and update on the inter-Ministry review mentioned last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: As MinLaw is uniquely positioned to consider the introduction of stricter enforcement within the community disputes framework, will the Minister review the prevailing policy to increase compliance of individuals with orders and agreements, and also provide us an update on the inter-Ministry review of the community dispute framework he mentioned last year?

sections.label: New civil enforcement measures
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to explain the new measures MinLaw is considering to improve the civil enforcement process in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: As such, can the Minister explain the new measures, that MinLaw is considering, to improve the civil enforcement process in Singapore?

sections.label: Unpaid worker with sick wife
sections.summary: The speaker says the judicial manager did not entertain him and he still works unpaid, hoping the company turns solvent, as his wife undergoes cancer treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The judicial manager did not entertain him and till this day, he is still working in the company without being paid his salary, in the hope that the company turns solvent, as he has a wife who is undergoing cancer treatment.

sections.label: Legal aid income thresholds
sections.summary: The threshold includes per capita income under $950 and savings under $10,000, and the Legal Aid Bureau launched Divorce AIDE last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The threshold includes having per capita income of less than $950 and savings of less than $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to this, I understand the Legal Aid Bureau has launched Divorce AIDE last year.

sections.label: Legal aid qualifying criteria
sections.summary: Qualifying criteria are household incomes under $1,500 and savings under $10,000, with exclusions including death-punishable and syndicated crime cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The qualifying criteria is for people with household incomes of less than $1,500 and savings of less than $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Certain types of cases are also excluded, including those punishable by death and those involving syndicated crimes.

sections.label: Public Defenders Office launch
sections.summary: The PDO was launched on 1 December 2022 with a higher means test of $1,500 per capita household income and wider offence coverage with exclusions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In such instances, while we have absolute and total faith in our Police and prosecutors in discharging their duties objectively and professionally, ensuring that accused persons have access to proper and professional legal representation will go a long way in assuring the public that we have a robust but fair criminal justice system that protects the interests of all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I was, therefore, very pleased that the PDO was launched on 1 December 2022, with a higher means test of $1,500 per capita household income and a wider coverage of offences, with exclusions.

sections.label: PDO update and Pro Bono SG funding
sections.summary: Parliament passed the Public Defenders Act and the PDO was set up last year; the Minister is asked for updates and on Pro Bono SG funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Parliament passed the Public Defenders Act and the PDO was set up last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update of the plans for the PDO this year, in terms of the number of staff it will hire and its expected caseload?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the PDO is taking on some functions of Pro Bono SG, could the Minister elaborate on whether the Ministry expects that it will continue funding Pro Bono SG in the long term and, if so, how it will ensure that it is not providing double funding to a Government body and an external private organisation carrying out similar functions?

sections.label: Professional Services ITM progress
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about the Professional Services Industry Transformation Map's progress, legal industry initiatives, and plans for a refresh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister elaborate on the progress of the Professional Services Industry Transformation Map (ITM) with particular focus on initiatives taken for the legal industry and whether there are plans for a refresh of the ITM?

sections.label: Legal Tech Platform update
sections.summary: The speaker says lawyers will not be replaced by technologies but those not using them will be, and asks for a Legal Tech Platform update.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Looking at the technologies currently available, I do not think lawyers will be replaced by them, but those that do not start using them eventually will be replaced by those who can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would also like to ask the Minister for an update on the Legal Tech Platform.

sections.label: In-house counsel training support
sections.summary: The speaker asks MinLaw to fund training and professional development for Singapore in-house counsels through SCCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The number of in-house counsels has outstripped the number of lawyers in practice to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: This presents a great opportunity for our Singapore in-house legal counsels to differentiate themselves in their skillset as they help businesses move confidently into the region, while also helping to bring back crucial work to our private practice lawyers and others in related fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: It is in this vein that I submit to MinLaw to provide even greater support and funding towards the training and professional development needs of in-house counsels in Singapore through SCCA.

sections.label: Lawyer admission regime changes
sections.summary: MinLaw accepted CPTL admission regime changes to be implemented this year; the speaker asks if feedback was received, including on low trainee allowance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, several changes to the admission regime recommended by the Committee for the Professional Training of Lawyers (CPTL) that were accepted by MinLaw will be implemented this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Has MinLaw received feedback from students, law firms and other stakeholders on the readiness and progress for the implementation this year, including concerns around low trainee allowance?

sections.label: Mitigating high prices review
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to clarify what it is considering to mitigate high prices and when the review will be completed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the meantime, could the Ministry clarify what it is considering to mitigate the high prices, and when the review will be completed?

sections.label: Religious institutions property conversion
sections.summary: High property prices are due in no small part to land cost; some religious institutions convert part of their property into profit-making activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: During the recent Motion on affordability and accessibility of the Housing and Development Board (HDB), it became amply clear that property prices are high in Singapore in no small part due to the cost of land.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The way some religious institutions have navigated this conundrum is to convert part of their operations into profit-making activities: they hive off part of their property for columbaria, childcare, coffee shops and carparks – I suppose you need the 4Cs in order to make the other big C, cash.

sections.label: Religious institutions land lease pricing
sections.summary: The speaker says religious institutions meet poorly valued societal needs and deserve special consideration for their class of land leases, as with mosques.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One solution is to recognise that religious institutions meet societal needs that are poorly valued by the market and, hence, are deserving of special consideration for their class of land leases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is the case for pricing for land for mosques, which Minister Shanmugam explained – in a response to Parliamentary Question filed by my hon friend Sylvia Lim – results in lower prices.

sections.label: State land interim use
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether state land not slated for development for 15 years and beyond can be put to longer-term interim use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can state land that is not slated for development for 15 years and beyond be put to longer-term interim use?

sections.label: Singapore small country size
sections.summary: Singapore faces challenges as a small country of about 730 square kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: One of the many challenges facing Singapore is that we are a small country of about 730 square kilometres in size.

sections.label: Digital conveyancing platform implementation
sections.summary: A vendor was appointed in January 2023 to develop an online platform for paperless digital conveyancing, due for full implementation in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Second Minister for Law, Mr Edwin Tong, announced in January 2023 the appointment of a vendor to develop the online platform to streamline the current paper-based conveyancing process and transform it into a fully integrated, efficient, transparent and paperless digital conveyancing process for all property transactions in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This platform is due to be fully implemented in 2026, which is barely three years from now.

sections.label: JTC leases environmental baseline studies
sections.summary: JTC leases typically require environmental baseline studies before approval can be granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Typically, JTC leases require environmental baseline studies to be carried out before approval can be granted.

sections.label: DCP announced in 2021
sections.summary: The DCP was announced during COS in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: The DCP was announced during COS in 2021.

sections.label: COVID-19 legislation amendments
sections.summary: Legislation was amended and the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act enacted, amended eight times, to refine Singapore's response to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our efforts provided reprieve to affected businesses and individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We amended various legislation and also enacted the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act – which itself, was amended eight times since it was passed – to refine Singapore's response to the evolving and developing situation as we faced COVID-19 and its impact on businesses.

sections.label: Electronic court proceedings, insolvency programme
sections.summary: Courts' powers to conduct proceedings electronically were made permanent, and features of the Simplified Insolvency Programme are being considered for permanent adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, we have made permanent, the powers of the Courts to conduct proceedings through electronic means, such as video conferencing in a variety of fashion, as Mr Pillai knows.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are also considering whether some features of the Simplified Insolvency Programme can be adopted permanently, something I spoke about in Parliament, not long ago.

sections.label: Sentencing Advisory Panel and PDO
sections.summary: The speakers will address themes and cuts raised by Members, including establishing the Sentencing Advisory Panel and the PDO and passing the Post-appeal Applications in Capital Cases Bill 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam and I will address these themes and also address, as far as we can, the cuts that have been raised by Members.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This included: establishing the Sentencing Advisory Panel and the PDO; and also passing the Post-appeal Applications in Capital Cases Bill 2022.

sections.label: Community neighbourly disputes mediation team
sections.summary: A team of dedicated personnel will be set up to leverage stronger laws and active facilitation to help neighbours resolve disputes upstream before they escalate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We live in an environment where we are close to one another and the best solution to dealing with community neighbourly disputes, is to find an amicable mediated position.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, going to be looking at setting up a team of dedicated personnel which will be able to leverage on stronger laws and more active facilitation to help neighbours resolve the issues upstream, before matters escalate and relationships deteriorate to an extent that, perhaps, matters become intransigent or deadlocked.

sections.label: Voluntary mediation cases settled at CMC
sections.summary: More than 80% of voluntary mediation cases handled at the CMC were successfully settled.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: More than 80% of the voluntary mediation cases handled at the CMC were successfully settled.

sections.label: Voluntary cases proceeding to mediation
sections.summary: Less than 30% of such voluntary cases proceed to mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To provide specific figures, less than 30% of such voluntary cases proceed to mediation.

sections.label: Mandatory mediation for community disputes
sections.summary: To improve early take-up of mediation, mediation will be mandated for three categories of cases, with penalties for not attending mandatory mediation for certain community disputes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And in addition, parties might think there is no issue to mediate; or they might think it is not effective at resolving the disputes between the parties; or they might decide to escalate the matter to CDRT without first attempting mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, to improve the take-up of mediation at an early stage, we plan to mandate mediation for three categories of cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, mediation would be mandatory for certain types of community disputes and penalties will be imposed for not attending mandatory mediation.

sections.label: Registering and enforcing mediated settlement agreements
sections.summary: A mechanism will be created for CMC-mediated settlement agreements to be registered and enforced as a CDRT Order if certain conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To give mediation more standing and teeth, we will also create a mechanism for settlement agreements mediated by the CMC to be registered and enforced as a CDRT Order, provided certain conditions are met.

sections.label: CDRT improvements and deterrence
sections.summary: The CDRT will remain a last resort, with improvements for laypeople, study of mental health-linked nuisance cases, and stronger deterrence of non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For these cases, the CDRT will continue to serve as an avenue of last resort.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will make improvements to address feedback that laypeople face in collecting evidence, which has been raised in this House before, and navigating the CDRT's process and procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, we are also studying how best to address cases where a person's act of nuisance may be linked to an underlying mental health condition.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Furthermore, there will also be stronger measures to deter non-compliance with the CDRT's orders.

sections.label: Pro Bono SG legal clinics
sections.summary: New CLCs run by Pro Bono SG were launched in January 2023, bringing legal services into the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One example is what Mr Raj Joshua Thomas spoke about, the new CLCs run by Pro Bono SG.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was launched recently in January 2023 and this effort brings legal services right into the heartlands.

sections.label: LTP adoption by firms
sections.summary: As of January 2023, the LTP has been adopted by 27 Singapore-based firms with around 550 Singapore-based users.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of January 2023, the LTP has been adopted by 27 Singapore-based firms, with around 550 Singapore-based users.

sections.label: Cloud-based template repository
sections.summary: The firm's templates are now in a cloud-based repository, preserving institutional knowledge and saving 50% of onboarding time for new matters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The firm's templates are now in a cloud-based repository, instead of the email archives of the individual lawyers – so that there is more institutional knowledge even when lawyers leave the firm and new ones come in.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This has saved 50% of the onboarding time for new matters.

sections.label: LTP system integration April
sections.summary: From April this year, the LTP will process information from systems such as eLitigation and ACRA and be integrated with Sign with Singpass.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, come April this year, the LTP will be able to process information from systems, such as eLitigation and the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA); and also integrated with Sign with Singpass.

sections.label: Industry-wide secondment programme
sections.summary: An industry-wide secondment programme will be launched to deepen lawyers' capabilities, targeting an intake of 30 lawyers a year at steady state.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, what we need to do – and in fact, what we have to do – is to re-double our efforts on developing our human talent, as much as we need to invest in technology.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will be launching an industry-wide secondment programme, which aims to deepen the capabilities of lawyers in important markets, as well as new or high growth areas, such as sustainability, technology and mergers and aquisitions (M&A).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are targeting to have an intake of 30 lawyers a year, at a steady state.

sections.label: Legal education system review
sections.summary: A Working Group comprising MinLaw, Judiciary, profession, law schools and legal education providers has been formed to conduct a holistic review of the legal education system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As the Chief Justice announced, at the Opening of the Legal Year (OLY) this year, a Working Group, comprising MinLaw, members of the Judiciary, the profession, law schools and legal education providers, has been formed to conduct a holistic review of our legal education system.

sections.label: Singapore-qualified practising lawyers numbers
sections.summary: The total number of Singapore-qualified practising lawyers rose gradually from around 5,400 practitioners in 2017 to around 6,400 practitioners in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If we take this account, then, there would, in fact, have been a gradual small increase in the total number of Singapore-qualified practising lawyers over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, to give Members some idea of the numbers, from around 5,400 practitioners in 2017 to around 6,400 practitioners in 2022.

sections.label: Bar admission and practice training changes
sections.summary: MinLaw previously announced uncoupling admission to the Bar from completing a practice training contract and lengthening the Practice Training Period from six months to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw previously announced the uncoupling of admission to the Bar from the completion of a practice training contract, and also the lengthening of the Practice Training Period from six months to one year.

sections.label: Deferral of Bar changes
sections.summary: The previously announced changes will be deferred and implemented from the 2024 session of the Part B of the Singapore Bar Examination onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With the recent resumption of travel and business activities, more time is needed to prepare for these changes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, these changes, that were announced previously, will be deferred and implemented from the 2024 session of the Part B of the Singapore Bar Examination onwards.

sections.label: Singapore IP Strategy 2030
sections.summary: MinLaw, MOF and MTI are driving the Singapore IP Strategy 2030, and this year the Intangibles Disclosure Framework will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw, MOF and MTI are driving the Singapore IP Strategy 2030, or SIPS 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As part of SIPS 2030, we have been working to support businesses to leverage their IA and IP for growth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we will be introducing the Intangibles Disclosure Framework.

sections.label: GoBusiness IP Grow platform
sections.summary: GoBusiness IP Grow, an enterprise-centric online platform, will be launched to help businesses understand IP needs, match them to IP services providers and provide one-stop access to enterprise IA and IP-related resources.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, we will launch GoBusiness IP Grow.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is an enterprise-centric online platform which will help businesses understand their IP needs based on their business activities; match businesses to appropriate IP services providers based on the particular business model they are practising and using, and also provide one-stop access to enterprise IA and IP-related resources.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We had, in fact, given a previous Parliamentary reply which Ms Lim also noted.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was noted then, and let me just reiterate, that we have been reviewing the land allocation and pricing framework for places of worship, to see how the price can be mitigated, bearing in mind the concerns that the Member raised.

sections.label: Religious organisations land price mitigation
sections.summary: The Government is working with affected religious organisations to mitigate land price increases, including offering short-term tenancy extensions pending a review.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the meantime, the Government has been working with affected religious organisations to assist them in mitigating the increase in land prices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, for instance, this would include offering the religious organisations a short-term tenancy extension, pending the outcome of this review that we are undertaking.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office criminal aid
sections.summary: The PDO, set up in December 2022, expanded criminal defence aid to the bottom 35% of resident households and received over 250 applications by 31 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The PDO, set up in December 2022, increases access to justice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The coverage of criminal defence aid has been expanded to the bottom 35% of resident households and covers offences in all but 10 Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2023, more than 250 applications have been received.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Of about 130 applications which have completed assessment, about 60 applications have been assessed to be eligible for criminal defence aid.

sections.label: Criminal and civil aid means test
sections.summary: The criminal defence aid means test threshold is PCHI $1,500 or the 35th percentile, while the civil defence aid threshold is PCHI $950 or the 25th percentile.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To Mr Nair's query, the criminal defence aid means test threshold is pegged at PCHI of $1,500, or the 35th percentile of households by income, while the civil defence aid means test is pegged at PCHI $950, or the 25th percentile of households by income.

sections.label: FJC e-service for simplified divorce
sections.summary: In 2022, the Family Justice Courts introduced an e-service allowing SRPs to e-file for simplified divorce without going to the CrimsonLogic Service Bureau.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2022, the Family Justice Courts (FJC) introduced an e-service that allows SRPs to e-file for simplified divorce, without having to go to the CrimsonLogic Service Bureau.

sections.label: Probate applications e-service target
sections.summary: A similar e-service for straightforward probate applications is targeted to be introduced by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Further, as Mr Murali Pillai alluded to, a similar e-service for straightforward probate applications is targeted to be introduced by 2023.
